```{r setup}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false

library(simmer)
library(here)

source(here('R/inputs.R'))     # Model Parameters
inputs <- modifyList(inputs,list(min_age = 20, maarrivalsage = 30))
source(here('R/main_loop.R'))  # Helper functions
source(here('R/discount.R'))   # Discounting functions

  
# Events (State Transitions)
source(here::here('R/event_death2.R'))
source(here::here('R/event_sick1.R'))
source(here::here('R/event_healthy.R'))

truncate_df <- function(df) {
  # Check if data frame has more than 10 rows
  if (nrow(df) <= 10) {
    # If 10 or fewer rows, convert all columns to character after rounding
    df_char <- df %>%
      mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ as.character(signif(., 3)))) %>%
      mutate(across(everything(), as.character))
    return(df_char)
  }
  
  # If more than 10 rows, select first 3 and last 3 rows
  first_three <- df[1:3, ]
  last_three <- df[(nrow(df)-2):nrow(df), ]
  
  # Convert all columns to character after rounding numeric columns to 3 significant digits
  first_three_char <- first_three %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ as.character(signif(., 4)))) %>%
    mutate(across(everything(), as.character))
  
  last_three_char <- last_three %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ as.character(signif(., 4)))) %>%
    mutate(across(everything(), as.character))
  
  # Create a row with "..." for all columns
  dots_row <- data.frame(matrix("...", nrow = 1, ncol = ncol(df)))
  names(dots_row) <- names(df)
  
  # Combine the rows: first 3 + dots row + last 3
  result <- rbind(first_three_char, dots_row, last_three_char)
  
  # Reset row names
  rownames(result) <- NULL
  
  return(result)
}  
# Resource or "Counters"
#
# These are used to track things that incur costs or qalys, or other
# things of which a count might be of interest.
# Infinite in quantity
counters <- c(
  "time_in_model",
  "death",
  "healthy",
  "sick1"
)
  
# Define starting state of patient
initialize_patient <- function(traj, inputs)
{
  traj                   |>
  seize("time_in_model") |>
  set_attribute("AgeInitial", function() sample(20:30, 1)) |>
  set_attribute("State", 0) |> # Patients start healthy
  seize("healthy") 
}

# Cleanup function if a termination occurs
# Good for releasing any seized resources based on state.
cleanup_on_termination <- function(traj)
{
  traj |> 
  release("time_in_model") |>
  branch( 
    function() get_attribute(env, "State")+1,
      continue = rep(TRUE, 3),
      trajectory() |> release("healthy"),
      trajectory() |> release("sick1"),
      trajectory() 
  )
}

terminate_simulation <- function(traj, inputs)
{
  traj |>
  branch( function() 1, 
          continue=FALSE,
          trajectory() |> cleanup_on_termination()
        )
}

# Main Event registry
event_registry <- list(
  list(name          = "Terminate at time horizon",
       attr          = "aTerminate",
       time_to_event = function(inputs) inputs$horizon-now(env),
       func          = terminate_simulation,
       reactive      = FALSE),
  list(name          = "Death",
       attr          = "aDeath",
       time_to_event = years_till_death,
       func          = death,
       reactive      = TRUE),
  list(name          = "Sick1",
       attr          = "aSick1",
       time_to_event = years_till_sick1,
       func          = sick1,
       reactive      = TRUE),
  list(name          = "Healthy",
       attr          = "aHealthy",
       time_to_event = years_till_healthy,
       func          = healthy,
       reactive      = TRUE)
)

cost_arrivals <- function(arrivals, inputs)
{
  arrivals$cost  <- 0  # Undiscounted costs are 0 to begin
  arrivals$dcost <- 0  # Discounted costs are 0 to begin
  
  selector = arrivals$resource == 'healthy'
  arrivals$cost[selector] <- inputs$c.H *
    (arrivals$end_time[selector] - arrivals$start_time[selector])
  arrivals$dcost[selector] <- discount_value(inputs$c.H,
    arrivals$start_time[selector], arrivals$end_time[selector],
    annual_rate = inputs$d.r)
  
  selector = arrivals$resource == 'sick1'
  arrivals$cost[selector] <- inputs$c.S1 *
    (arrivals$end_time[selector] - arrivals$start_time[selector])
  arrivals$dcost[selector] <- discount_value(inputs$c.S1,
    arrivals$start_time[selector], arrivals$end_time[selector],
    annual_rate = inputs$d.r)
 
  arrivals
}

qaly_arrivals <- function(arrivals, inputs)
{
  arrivals$qaly  <- 0  # No qaly yet
  arrivals$dqaly <- 0  # No discounted qaly either
  
  selector <- arrivals$resource == 'healthy'
  arrivals$qaly[selector] <-
    inputs$u.H*
     (arrivals$end_time[selector] - arrivals$start_time[selector])
  arrivals$dqaly[selector] <- 
      discount_value(inputs$u.H, 
                     arrivals$start_time[selector],
                     arrivals$end_time[selector],annual_rate = inputs$d.r)
  
  selector <- arrivals$resource == 'sick1'
  arrivals$qaly[selector] <-
    inputs$u.S1*
     (arrivals$end_time[selector] - arrivals$start_time[selector])
  arrivals$dqaly[selector] <- 
      discount_value(inputs$u.S1, 
                     arrivals$start_time[selector],
                     arrivals$end_time[selector],annual_rate = inputs$d.r)
  
  arrivals
}

# This does a single DES run versus the defined inputs.
des_run <- function(inputs)
{
  env  <<- simmer("SickSicker")
  traj <- des(env, inputs)
  env |> 
    create_counters(counters) |>
    add_generator("patient", traj, at(rep(0, inputs$N)), mon=2) |>
    run(inputs$horizon+1/365) |> # Simulate just past horizon (in years)
    wrap()
        
  get_mon_arrivals(env, per_resource = T) 
}

des_run2 <- function(inputs)
{
  env  <<- simmer("SickSicker")
  traj <- des(env, inputs)
  env |> 
    create_counters(counters) |>
    add_generator("patient", traj, at(rep(0, inputs$N)), mon=2) |>
    run(inputs$horizon+1/365) |> # Simulate just past horizon (in years)
    wrap()
        
  get_mon_arrivals(env, per_resource = T)  |>
    cost_arrivals(inputs = inputs) |>
    qaly_arrivals(inputs = inputs)
}

set.seed(1)
inputs <- modifyList(inputs,list(horizon=   110))
res_model2 <- des_run(inputs) 
res_model2b <- des_run2(inputs) 
```

:::{.cr-section}

@cr-petrisick Our next objective is to build in a single [**sick**]{style="color:crimson"} health state. 

:::{#cr-petrisick}
![](images/petri-model4.png){fig-align="center"}
:::

[@cr-petrisick]{pan-to="90%, 50%" scale-by="2.8"} Notice that the sick state will 
allow for disease recovery (i.e., a return to the [**Healthy**]{style="color:#6A6599FF"} state). 


[@cr-petrisick]{pan-to="90%, 50%" scale-by="2.8"} We therefore need to add in two new transitions: (1) becoming ill; and (2) disease recovery. 


@cr-inputs2 Let's now re-define the model inputs.

[@cr-inputs2]{highlight="6"} We include an annual hazard rate of progression from [**Healthy**]{style="color:#6A6599FF"} to [**Sick**]{style="color:#6A6599FF"}.


[@cr-inputs2]{highlight="7"} As well as an annual disease recovery rate. 

[@cr-inputs2]{highlight="8"} The hazard rate of death from Healthy remains the same. 


[@cr-inputs2]{highlight="9"} But patients in the sick state have a higher rate
of death, as summarized by a hazard ratio. 

[@cr-inputs2]{highlight="11-15"} Later we'll build in some accounting of costs 
and quality of life, so we include cost and QALY parameters in the inputs
as well. 

[@cr-inputs2]{highlight="18"} We'll also cover point and interval discounting
when we come to outcome estimation. 

:::{#cr-inputs2}
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| code-line-numbers: true
#| 
inputs <- list(
    N       = 1,  # Total number of patients to simulate. 
    horizon = 110,  # Time horizon (years)
    min_age = 20,
    max_age = 30,
    r.HS1  =  0.15,   # Disease Onset Rate / year    (H  -> S)
    r.S1H  =  0.7,    # Recovery Rate / year         (S -> H)
    r.HD   =  0.005,  # Healthy to Dead rate / year  (H  -> D)
    hr.S1D =  3,      # Hazard ratio in S1 vs healthy 
    
    c.H    =  2000,      # Healthy individuals 
    c.S1   =  4000,      # Sick individuals in S1
    
    u.H    =     1.00,   # Healthy
    u.S1   =     0.80,   # S1
    
    # Cycle => 1 year
    d.r    =     0.03   # Discount Rate
)
```
:::

[@cr-initialize]{highlight="1-6"} Let's add the sick state to the counters. 

[@cr-initialize]{highlight="5"} Note that we index sick with a value of 1. That's 
because **simmer** requires that health states be tracked using a numeric
categorical variable that starts with zero. 


[@cr-initialize]{highlight="8-16"} We next add code initilise all patients into 
the healthy state.

[@cr-initialize]{highlight="14"} We do this be setting the `state` attribute value
to zero upon inilialisation of the patient. 

[@cr-initialize]{highlight="15"} We'll also want to track the amount of time spent
in the healthy state later, for estimation of quality-of-life. So we need to add time in the 
[**healthy**]{style="color:#6A6599FF"} state to our resource counters. 

:::{#cr-initialize}

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| code-line-numbers: true
#| 
counters <- c(
  "time_in_model",
  "death",
  "healthy",
  "sick1"
)
  
# Define starting state of patient
initialize_patient <- function(traj, inputs)
{
  traj                   |>
  seize("time_in_model") |>
  set_attribute("AgeInitial", function() sample(20:30, 1)) |>
  set_attribute("State", 0) |> # Patients start healthy
  seize("healthy") 
}
```

:::


@cr-deathevent2 Because the death rate now depends on health state, we amend
our `time_to_death` function to draw a death time depending on whether the patient 
is [**Healthy**]{style="color:#6A6599FF"} or [**Sick**]{style="color:#6A6599FF"}.

:::{#cr-deathevent2}
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| code-line-numbers: true
years_till_death <- function(inputs)
{
  state <- get_attribute(env, "State")
  rate <- inputs$r.HD
  if(state == 1) rate <- rate * inputs$hr.S1D # Deal with Sick1 Hazard Ratio
  rexp(1, rate)
}
```

:::

@cr-sickevent2 The function that draws years till sick uses a draw from the
exponential distribution, and only sets a value within the simulation time
horizon if the patient is in the [**healthy**]{style="color:#6A6599FF"} state. 

:::{#cr-sickevent2}
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| code-line-numbers: true
years_till_sick1 <- function(inputs)
{
  state <- get_attribute(env, "State") 
  if(state == 0) # 0 => Healthy
  {
    rexp(1,inputs$r.HS1)
  } else
  {
    inputs$horizon+1 # Past end of simulation time
  }
}

```

:::

@cr-sickevent2b Once the patient transitions into the **sick** state, we reset her 
state attribute to a value of 1 (i.e., sick). 

[@cr-sickevent2b]{highlight="5,6"} She also releases the `healthy` resource and 
seizes the `sick` resouce. Again, this facilitates tracking total amount of time
in each health state. 

:::{#cr-sickevent2b}
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| code-line-numbers: true
sick1 <- function(traj, inputs)
{
  traj                      |> 
  set_attribute("State", 1) |> # 1 => Sick 1 (S1)
  release('healthy')        |> # Track state change for tally later
  seize('sick1')
}

```

:::

[@cr-petrisick]{pan-to="90%, 60%" scale-by="2.8"} Recall that in this model, patients can recover and become healthy 
again. 


@cr-healthy2 To allow for this, we need to define a function for **time to healthy** 
and a function that releases the [**sick**]{style="color:#79AF97FF"} resource and re-seizes [**healthy**]{style="color:#79AF97FF"}.

:::{#cr-healthy2}
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| code-line-numbers: true
years_till_healthy <- function(inputs)
{
  state <- get_attribute(env, "State") 
  if(state == 1) # 1 => Sick 1
  {
    rexp(1,inputs$r.S1H)
  } else
  {
    inputs$horizon+1 # Past end of simulation time
  }
}

healthy <- function(traj, inputs)
{
  traj                      |> 
  set_attribute("State", 0) |> # 0 => Healthy (H)
  seize('healthy')          |>
  release('sick1')
}
```

:::

@cr-cleanup2 We need to also amend our **cleanup** function so that it releases
the [**healthy**]{style="color:#79AF97FF"} resource (if healthy) and [**sick**]{style="color:#79AF97FF"} resource (if sick) at the
termination of the model. 

:::{#cr-cleanup2}
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| code-line-numbers: true
cleanup_on_termination <- function(traj)
{
  traj |> 
  release("time_in_model") |>
  branch( 
    function() get_attribute(env, "State")+1,
      continue = rep(TRUE, 3),
      trajectory() |> release("healthy"),
      trajectory() |> release("sick1"),
      trajectory() 
  )
}
```

:::

@cr-registry2 Finally, we amend our **event registry** so that our model output
records events for becoming ill and healthy. 

:::{#cr-registry2}
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| code-line-numbers: true
event_registry <- list(
  list(name          = "Terminate at time horizon",
       attr          = "aTerminate",
       time_to_event = function(inputs) inputs$horizon-now(env),
       func          = terminate_simulation,
       reactive      = FALSE),
  list(name          = "Death",
       attr          = "aDeath",
       time_to_event = years_till_death,
       func          = death,
       reactive      = TRUE),
  list(name          = "Sick1",
       attr          = "aSick1",
       time_to_event = years_till_sick1,
       func          = sick1,
       reactive      = TRUE),
  list(name          = "Healthy",
       attr          = "aHealthy",
       time_to_event = years_till_healthy,
       func          = healthy,
       reactive      = TRUE)
)

```

:::

@cr-Rmodel2result With the simple Healthy-Sick-Dead model built, let's now turn to outcome estimation. 

[@cr-inputs2]{highlight="11-15"} Recall that earlier, we included cost and utility weights in the inputs. 

[@cr-desrun2]{highlight="12-13"} Outcome estimation takes place after the model has run all patients. We do it by simply calculating and adding **cost** and **QALY** columns to the model output. 

[@cr-desrun2] We'll now define two functions, `cost_arrivals()` and `qaly_arrivals()` that take care of this process. 

[@cr-desrun2]{highlight="12-13"} These functions will be tucked into the very end of the `des_run()` function we defined that runs the simulation model. 

:::{#cr-desrun2}
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| code-line-numbers: true
des_run <- function(inputs)
{
  env  <<- simmer("SickSicker")
  traj <- des(env, inputs)
  env |> 
    create_counters(counters) |>
    add_generator("patient", traj, at(rep(0, inputs$N)), mon=2) |>
    run(inputs$horizon+1/365) |> # Simulate just past horizon (in years)
    wrap()
        
  get_mon_arrivals(env, per_resource = T) |>
    cost_arrivals(inputs) |> 
    qaly_arrivals(inputs) 
}
```

:::

:::{#cr-costarrivals2}
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| code-line-numbers: true
cost_arrivals <- function(arrivals, inputs)
{
  arrivals$cost  <- 0  # Undiscounted costs are 0 to begin
  arrivals$dcost <- 0  # Discounted costs are 0 to begin
  
  selector = arrivals$resource == 'healthy'
  arrivals$cost[selector] <- inputs$c.H *
    (arrivals$end_time[selector] - arrivals$start_time[selector])
  arrivals$dcost[selector] <- discount_value(inputs$c.H,
    arrivals$start_time[selector], arrivals$end_time[selector],
    annual_rate = inputs$d.r)
  
  selector = arrivals$resource == 'sick1'
  arrivals$cost[selector] <- inputs$c.S1 *
    (arrivals$end_time[selector] - arrivals$start_time[selector])
  arrivals$dcost[selector] <- discount_value(inputs$c.S1,
    arrivals$start_time[selector], arrivals$end_time[selector],
    annual_rate = inputs$d.r)
 
  arrivals
}
```

[@cr-costarrivals2]{highlight="4,9,10,11,16,17,18"} Let's now discuss discounting in DES model outputs. 

@cr-discount We have created a helper function `discount_value()` that takes care of continuous-time discounting 
for you. 

@cr-discount Many approaches use the power definition of discounting, which in R utilises “^” operator.  This limits the numerical stable range of the function. 

@cr-discount Our function uses the exponential formulation with a greater numerical stability. The function also does point discounting or time period (i.e., integrated area) discounting.

:::{#cr-discount}
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| code-line-numbers: true
discount_value <- function(value, t_A, t_B=NULL, annual_rate=0.03, scale=1)
{
  # Scale to time step
  if(scale != 1)
  {
    t_A <- t_A / scale
    if(!is.null(t_B)) t_B <- t_B / scale
  }
  
  # Convert discount to continuous exponential rate
  r <- -log(1+annual_rate) 

  if(is.null(t_B))
  { # Point estimate at t_B
    value*exp(r*t_A)
  } else 
  { # Analytic integral of curve
    (value/r)*(exp(r*t_B)-exp(r*t_A))
  }
}
```

:::

@cr-discountex For example, suppose we want to discount the value of 1, which occurs at *precisely* one year in the future. For example, this could be a one-time treatment cost. 

:::{#cr-discountex}
```{r}
#| echo: true
discount_value(
  value = 1, 
  t_A = 1, 
  annual_rate = 0.03
)
```

:::


@cr-discountex2 Now suppose we want to discount the value 1 over the time period 
$t=0$ to $t=1$. For example, this type of discounting would apply for time spent
in a health state. 

:::{#cr-discountex2}
```{r}
#| echo: true
discount_value(
  value = 1, 
  t_A = 0, 
  t_B = 1, 
  annual_rate = 0.03
)
```

:::


[@cr-costarrivals2]{highlight="9,10,11,16,17,18"}  Our cost calculation approach applies the `discount_value()` 
function to all time periods to calculate discounted costs. 


@cr-qalyarrivals2 We define a similar `qaly_arrivals()` function to calculate 
quality of life based on utility weights. 

[@cr-qalyarrivals2]{highlight="8,17"} The only major difference is that we multiply 
time in each health state with its corresponding utility weight. 

:::{#cr-qalyarrivals2}
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| code-line-numbers: true
qaly_arrivals <- function(arrivals, inputs)
{
  arrivals$qaly  <- 0  # No qaly yet
  arrivals$dqaly <- 0  # No discounted qaly either
  
  selector <- arrivals$resource == 'healthy'
  arrivals$qaly[selector] <-
    inputs$u.H*
     (arrivals$end_time[selector] - arrivals$start_time[selector])
  arrivals$dqaly[selector] <- 
      discount_value(inputs$u.H, 
                     arrivals$start_time[selector],
                     arrivals$end_time[selector],annual_rate = inputs$d.r)
  
  selector <- arrivals$resource == 'sick1'
  arrivals$qaly[selector] <-
    inputs$u.S1*
     (arrivals$end_time[selector] - arrivals$start_time[selector])
  arrivals$dqaly[selector] <- 
      discount_value(inputs$u.S1, 
                     arrivals$start_time[selector],
                     arrivals$end_time[selector],annual_rate = inputs$d.r)
  
  arrivals
}
```
:::
